clue.text: Drug user did wrong in law

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the word for law

parts.note: an act is a law passed by a parliament

indicators.note: done wrong, the three letters of did are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A drug user broke the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did wrong in law' reads as a crime, but 'wrong' shuffles DID into DDI, which 'in' sets inside ACT, as in an Act of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hooked on narcotics is called an addict.

clue.text: Tied up at work acquiring proficiency

indicators.note: work here means to rework or knead, so the letters of tied up at are rearranged

explanation.surface: Busy at the office while gaining skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is the anagram signal on TIED UP AT; 'acquiring' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural ability or talent for doing something well is a kind of skill.

clue.text: A way to serve potatoes, just stuffed with game

indicators.note: stuffed with means the word for just is filled with the word for game

parts.note: due means just or deserved, as in one's due reward
chess is a board game

explanation.surface: A recipe for potatoes, simply stuffed with game birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' suggests pheasant, but it is chess. Duchesse potatoes are mashed, piped and baked.
explanation.definitionFit: Mashed potato mixed with egg, piped into rosettes and baked is a classic French style.

parts.note: inside is slang for being in prison, so this is where an inmate sleeps

explanation.surface: Indoor lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside is British slang for in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner's small room in a jail is the lodging of someone who is locked up.

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wildly changed, so the letters of praised a are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lavishly praised a marvellous garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' looks like praise for the garden, but it is the anagram signal working on PRAISED A.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the Garden of Eden in the Bible, so the word can mean a garden.

clue.text: Performed with a high degree of skill

definitions.meaning: carried out or achieved, as a task

definitions.text: with a high degree of skill

explanation.surface: Played very expertly.
explanation.definitionFit: A completed task was achieved, and a gifted pianist is talented: the word covers both.

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Two cats having a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' suggests a fight between cats, but it means a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiniest particle or bit of something, as in not an iota, is a small fragment.

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of region are rearranged

explanation.surface: An area that has unfortunately been left uncared for.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay no attention to something is to disregard it, a verb sense.

clue.text: Make a mistake and run for it

parts.note: to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Blundering and then fleeing the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run for it' reads as fleeing, but means a short trip to fetch something.
explanation.definitionFit: A short trip to fetch or deliver something, such as a dash to the shop, is a task of that kind.

clue.text: It's used to lift — or bring down

definitions.meaning: lifting gear such as ropes and pulleys, as in block and ...
to stop a player in football or rugby by bringing them to the ground

explanation.surface: A piece of kit that both raises things and knocks them over.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means hoisting gear on ships and also a move that fells an opponent in sport.

definitions.meaning: a sailing vessel with fore-and-aft rigging
a large glass of beer or sherry, which is often handed over a pub counter

explanation.surface: A vessel that regularly sails over the sandbar at a harbour mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar looks like a harbour sandbar, but it is a pub counter: in Britain the word also names a tall glass for sherry or beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a two-masted sailing vessel and also a large drinking glass served at a pub.

parts.note: mayonnaise is a salad dressing
down means lower, as in further down

explanation.surface: A mayonnaise brand drops in the ratings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like a score, but it is a scolding, from the verb rate, to berate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating in this old sense is a severe scolding, and a dressing-down is a reprimand.

definitions.meaning: finished level in a contest, a draw

explanation.surface: A team destined to finish level on points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but 'Bound' is one definition and 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted string holds a parcel fast, and teams finishing level on points have drawn.

indicators.note: in places the single letter for the monarch within the word for temporary quarters

parts.note: a camp is a set of tents or huts used for a short stay
R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: Confining a king to a tented camp.
explanation.definitionFit: To hamper or confine someone is to hem them in, a verb sense of the word.

parts.note: one architect famed for London churches shares his name with a tiny bird that builds a nest

explanation.surface: Someone who builds both churches and nests.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral and many London churches; the same name belongs to a small brown songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird of that name builds a domed nest, and the architect of that name built St Paul's Cathedral.

clue.text: Vehicle holds up progress? Not true

indicators.note: holds means the vehicle word contains the other piece

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: go means progress, as in a project on the go

explanation.surface: A broken-down bus is holding up traffic, or so it is claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds up progress' reads as a traffic jam, but 'up' turns GO into OG, and 'holds' puts it inside BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fake or counterfeit is not genuine, as a sham claim is.

indicators.note: say means the word for skewer is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a stake is a pointed stick, like a skewer

explanation.surface: Meat on a skewer, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick slice of beef cut for grilling is a cut of meat.

clue.text: Gloomy record playing far on into the night

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
on means playing, as a record that is on
so late describes an hour far into the night

explanation.surface: Feeling down while records play deep into the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is deeply unhappy and cannot be cheered is described this way.

clue.text: Sail north, but ordered into port

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailing north, but commanded to head into a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' reads as commanded, but it is the anagram signal on SAIL, N and BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish city on the Bosporus is a major seaport.

indicators.note: about means the subsidy word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a grant is a subsidy
to die is to expire

explanation.surface: A bank's subsidy is about to run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to expire' looks like one phrase meaning soon to end; 'about' is the container signal and 'to expire' gives DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank in the sense of a slope rises at an angle, and an incline is a gradient.

clue.text: He received his final rents mid-month

definitions.text: He received his final rents mid-month

parts.words: He received his final rents mid-month
parts.note: rents are not payments but tears or stab wounds, received on the Ides of March, the middle of that month

explanation.surface: A landlord collecting his last rent payments halfway through the month.
explanation.walkthrough: Rents means rips or wounds; the Roman leader was stabbed to death on the Ides of March, 15 March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman dictator was assassinated with daggers on the Ides of March, the middle of the month.

indicators.note: built, after the re of re-built, means put together anew, so the letters of pubs and re are rearranged

explanation.surface: Refurbished pubs giving drinkers more options.
explanation.walkthrough: 're-built' splits: its RE joins PUBS as fodder, and 'built' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Choice as an adjective means of top quality, like excellent.

indicators.note: takes, with in, means the cleric word takes another piece inside it
in completes takes ... in, the cleric taking the other word inside

parts.note: a dean is a senior clergyman

explanation.surface: A modest churchman offers me lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' looks like an adjective describing the cleric, but it is a verb: to lower someone's dignity.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower someone's dignity or standing is to abase them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Employer provides a course in the city

indicators.note: in places the compass direction within the ancient city's name

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city in Mesopotamia, a crossword favourite
SE, south-east, is a compass course to steer

explanation.surface: A boss lays on a training course in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the city' tempts with EC for the City of London, but it is UR; 'course' is a compass heading, not a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who employs a tool or method makes use of it, so an employer here is one who uses.

indicators.note: in places the word for about within the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
re means about or concerning, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Arriving roughly in time for a football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Two accounts that correspond or tally are said to match, a verb sense.

indicators.note: into places the numeral one inside the word for residence

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newcomer finally settled into a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that has been settled has been paid off, the same past sense.

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to abut is to touch, as neighbouring land does

explanation.surface: Polishing up some brass ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touch up' looks like a phrase meaning retouch; 'up' reverses ABUT. 'some brass' is one member of the brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: The large low-pitched valved horn is one instrument of an orchestra's brass section.

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, the British volunteer reserve
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: An army squad's vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab hired for a journey is a means of getting about.

clue.text: Someone must have been willing to appoint him

definitions.text: Someone must have been willing to appoint him

parts.words: Someone must have been willing to appoint him
parts.note: willing is read as making a will: the person who drew up a will names the official who carries it out

explanation.surface: Somebody must have been keen enough to give him the job.
explanation.walkthrough: Willing seems to mean eager, but it means making a will, in which the testator names who will carry it out.
explanation.definitionFit: The person named in a will to carry out its terms is appointed by the testator.

parts.note: pretty can mean attractive or fairly: a decorative trinket that serves no purpose

explanation.surface: Something that is fairly useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' reads as 'fairly', but it also means attractive: a showy trinket of no use.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheap showy trinket or Christmas tree ornament is decorative but of little value.

indicators.note: the head of the word bandage is its first letter

parts.note: and means with or together with
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Wrapping a wound with a girl's headscarf.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly coloured square of cloth tied round the head or neck is a kind of headscarf.

clue.text: I'll have a gamble about private accommodation

indicators.note: about places one piece around another, here the wager around the contraction

parts.note: to bet is to have a gamble
the contraction gives its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to have a flutter on renting a private flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like personal, but it is an army private, a soldier: the answer is lodging assigned to troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier's lodging in a civilian house is a billet, and a private is a rank-and-file soldier.
